identity.title: Cavity and other radial substructures in the disk around HD 97048

paper_type_evidence.quote: We image the disk around HD 97048 using ALMA at 0.85 mm and 2.94 mm, and ATCA (multiple frequencies) observations.

evidence.quote: HD 97048 is a 3 Myr (cite: 2006Sci...314..621L), 2.5 M$_\ensuremath{\odot}$ (cite: 2007A&A...470..625D) HAeBe with spectral type A0 at a distance of 158$^{+17}_{-14}$ parsec (cite: 2007A&A...474..653V).

question.value: Does the Herbig Ae/Be disk around HD 97048 host the predicted ~34 au central cavity, and what is its radial (sub)mm structure?

evidence.quote: We aim to resolve the 34$\pm$ 4 au central cavity predicted by Maaskant et al. (2013) and to investigate the structure of the disk.
(PI: G van der Plas, Program ID 2013.1.00658.S)
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA# 2013.1.00658.S and 2012.1.00031.S.

evidence.quote: We image the disk around HD 97048 using ALMA at 0.85 mm and 2.94 mm, and ATCA (multiple frequencies) observations.

evidence.quote: These two TDM spectral windows were centred st 345.8 GHz and 356.7 GHz.
The fourth spectral window was configured in FDM to target the J=1-0 line and centered at 105.2 GHz, with a spectral resolution of 159 m s$^{-1}$ and a total bandwidth of 0.117 GHz.
The array configuration provided baselines ranging between 15.8 and 462.9 meters.
which results in a restoring beam of respectively 0.63$''$ $\times$ 0.36$''$ at PA = 19$^\circ$ (Briggs)

ALMA Early Science Cycle 1 observations were conducted on 1 December 2013 with 72.6 seconds of total time on HD 97048

analysis_steps.goal: Fit continuum size, flux, inclination and PA

method.value: Fit a disk (ALMA) or Gaussian/point (ATCA) to visibilities

evidence.quote: We extract the size and flux of HD 97048 by using the CASA task *uvmodelfit* to fit a disk to the visibility data

analysis_steps.goal: Image continuum and reconstruct super-resolved images

method.value: CLEAN with several weightings, long-baseline imaging, and MEM (uvmem)

evidence.quote: We use the *uvmem* algorithm (cite: 2006ApJ...639..951C; 2015ApJ...811...92C; 2015ApJ...812..126C)

analysis_steps.goal: Radial surface brightness profile and power-law fits

method.value: Deproject superuniform image, collapse radially, fit three power laws a0 r^a1 between 0.3 and 2.6 arcsec

evidence.quote: We fit a power law to these 3 sections of the form *a$_0$ $\times$ r$^{a_1}$* between 0.3 and 2.6$''$, separated at 1.05$''$ and 1.95$''$.

analysis_steps.goal: Model gap vs ring with radiative transfer

method.value: MCFOST model with Gaussian gap or extra ring, simobserve to visibilities, CLEAN, compare visibilities and images

evidence.quote: we use the CASA tasks *simobserve* to convert the image into visibilities, as would be observed with a similar antenna configuration and on-sky properties as for our ALMA band 7 observations.
we do not determine confidence intervals for our derived parameters.

method.value: Linear least squares fit to 1-10 mm SED; beyond 10 mm subtract extrapolated power law and fit

evidence.quote: A linear least squares fit to the 1–10 mm portion of the SED yields a spectral index $\alpha$ (where $F \propto \nu^\alpha$) of 3.1 $\pm$ 0.1.

analysis_steps.goal: Line moment maps, systemic velocity and emitting radii

method.value: Moment 0, 1, 8 maps; radius from line wing half width assuming Keplerian rotation, i=41.4 deg, 2.5 Msun

evidence.quote: These values can be translated to an emitting radius of 13.4 and 27.0 au, assuming the gas is in Keplerian rotation in a disk inclined by 41.4$^\circ$ around a 2.5 M$_{\odot}$ star.

method.value: Optically thin isothermal dust mass at 43 GHz

evidence.quote: We estimate the emitting dust mass at 43 GHz, by assuming the disk is isothermal and optically thin

assumptions.value: T_dust=15 K, gas-to-dust 100, kappa_1.3mm=2.3 with kappa~nu^0.4

evidence.quote: Using a gas-to-dust ratio of 100, these assumptions result in a total disk mass of 0.0082 M$_\ensuremath{\odot}$
We used the standard reduction tools within the CASA package to calibrate and combine the data.

findings_qualitative.value: The 34 GHz ATCA image does not show the cavity, likely because unresolved free-free emission fills it in

evidence.quote: The disk cavity is not detected at 9 mm because free-free emission from the star fills in the cavity at our spatial resolution.

findings_qualitative.value: J=4-3 velocity map shows non-Keplerian 's'-shaped pattern inside the cavity

evidence.quote: shows an ‘s’ shaped pattern, characteristic for non-keplerian in-falling gas or an inner disk warp

claims.hypothesis: HD 97048 has a dust cavity as predicted
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 7 imaging, MEM, and MCFOST modelling
claims.finding: A cavity is resolved, with size varying with wavelength/tracer

evidence.quote: A central cavity in the disk around HD 97048 is resolved with a 40-46 au radius.

claims.hypothesis: Additional radial structure is a gap or a ring
claims.experiment: MCFOST gap and ring models compared to Band 7 data
claims.result: Both reproduce data similarly; gap at ~90 au or ring at ~150 au

evidence.quote: We find that both tested underlying brightness distributions produce comparable matches to the observations.

claims.hypothesis: Gas inside the cavity is non-Keplerian, suggesting a companion
claims.finding: Suggests orbiting body or inner disk warp

evidence.quote: we cannot distinguish between both scenarios.
is consistent with a dust distribution in the disk with relatively large grains.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Point plus disk and point plus ring models at 33/35 and 38/40 GHz were unsatisfactory

evidence.quote: Models for a ‘point plus disk’ and ‘point plus ring’ were also tried at 33/35 and 38/40 GHz, but the results were unsatisfactory

limitations_admitted.value: Limited resolution cannot distinguish gap from ring

evidence.quote: the limited spatial resolution of our observations does not allow us to differentiate between the presence of a gap or a ring

referee_caveats_inferred: Model fits are manual with no uncertainties
Foreground absorption affects CO line cores
Resolution inside the cavity is coarse for kinematic claims
Free-free fill-in inferred from sparse, multi-epoch ATCA data
